lines: HubSpot co-founder and CTO Dharmesh Shah argues startups should stay off the 'Yellow Brick Road' frontier AI labs are racing down and instead target specific, high-value workflows where the labs face structural or incentive constraints.
He points to record business formation, with over 70% of new ventures expected to stay one-person businesses, as a large, underserved market for specialized AI-native software.

Shah says durable AI products combine structured systems of record with unstructured context, a 'second brain' for agentic workflows, and use cheap deterministic queries for retrieval while reserving costly inference for real reasoning.
In his view the interface is only a means to an end: lasting advantage comes from the underlying data, customer context and delivered outcomes, not from wrapping a model.

Drawing on HubSpot's path from marketing suite to all-in-one CRM, he advises starting with a narrow wedge on a fragmented pain point, running fast iteration cycles, and keeping a 'startup within a startup' mindset.
title: HubSpot’s Co-Founder on Finding Your Next Startup Idea
